This example is for the IVR8 (Icepack Vehicle Router 8) model. IVR8 is an extension to IVR7 with compartment modelling added. This is useful for tanker fleets or axel load-constraint modelling. 

In this example, we'll use a simple one-rack compartment configuration and a single vehicle with added allowable-compartment assignments (i.e. which jobs may be assigned to which compartments) to demonstrate how to use compartment constraints on a particular model.

### Data 

```{r}

data <- read.csv('../sample_data/publist_orders.csv')[1:9, ] 

number_pubs <- nrow(data)

```

The data used in this example is a list of `r number_pubs` pubs in Dublin, Ireland with their associated X and Y coordinates, pickup and dropoff times, and quantities (amount added to a vehicle at each location). There are 8 pickups and 8 dropoffs.

```{r}
#| echo: false
#| output: false

if(!("pacman" %in% rownames(installed.packages()))){
  install.packages("pacman")
}

library(pacman)
p_load(tidyverse)
p_load(DT)
p_load(dplyr)
```

```{r}

data <- data %>% mutate(across(2:3, ~ format(round(.x, digits=5), nsmall = 5))) 

datatable(data, colnames = c("Pub Name (id)",
                           "X-Coordinate (X)",
                           "Y-Coordinate (Y)",
                           "Pickup Time (pickupTime)",
                           "Dropoff Time (dropoffTime)",
                           "Quantity (quantity)")
                           , options = list(dom = 't', scrollY = "200px", pageLength=nrow(data), columnDefs = list(list(className = 'dt-right', targets = 2:6))))

```

### Running the example

An R script with all the lines needed to run the example can be found [here](https://github.com/Icepack-co/examples/blob/master/R/ivr8-3-advanced.R).

The example uses the **iceR** package which will first need to be installed (see information [here](https://github.com/Icepack-co/iceR)) and then loaded. Helper functions are also provided in a separate file and need to be read in.

```{r}
#| echo: true
#| output: false
library(iceR)

source('ivr8-model-helper.R')

```


Execute the example as follows:

1. **Create an apiHelper object with the model type you'd like to solve**

```{r}
#| echo: true
#| output: false
api <- new("apiHelper", modelType = 'ivr8-yni1c9k2swof', configFile = '../config.json')
```


2. **Create the model and add some data to it**

```{r}
#| echo: true
#| output: false

# Create the model
sr <- new (IVR8.SolveRequest)
sr$model <- new (IVR8.Model)

# Load the data (we're going to use location 1 as the depot and locations 2 to 9 as the stops)
data <- read.csv('../sample_data/publist_orders.csv')[1:9, ]

# Configure the model and add the data to it (See ivr8-model-helper.R for details around some of the methods used below)

# (a) Dimensions, Locations, Jobs, Vehicles, Vehicle Classes and Vehicle Cost Classes (see the IVR7 example for more details around this)
sr$model$dimensions <- make_distance_time_cap_dims()
sr$model$locations <- make_locations(data)
sr$model$jobs <- make_job_time_cap(data, src = rep(1, nrow(data) - 1), dest = 2:nrow(data))
sr$model$vehicleCostClasses <- make_vcc_simple('vcc1', 1000, 0.01, 0.01, 0.01, 1, 3)
sr$model$vehicleClasses <- make_vc_simple('vc1', 1, 1, 1, 1)
sr$model$vehicles <- make_vehicle_cap("vehicle_1", 'vc1', 'vcc1',
                                   2000, # the vehicle capacity
                                   data$id[1], # start location
                                   data$id[1], # end location
                                   7*60,  # 7 AM
                                   18*60) # 6 PM

# (b) Compartments and Compartment Sets
# We're going to assume that we have a vehicle which is layed out as follows:
#  Lower Rack  [ ] [ ] [ ] [ ]  500kg per "compartment"  c1, c2, c3, c4

sr$model$compartments <- list()
for(i in 1:4){
  comp <- new (IVR8.Compartment)
  comp$id <- paste0("c", i)
  comp$capacities <- new (IVR8.Compartment.Capacity)
  comp$capacities[[1]]$dimensionId <- "capacity"
  comp$capacities[[1]]$capacity <- 500 # top rack
  sr$model$compartments  <- append(sr$model$compartments, comp)
}

# Now we can go back through the tasks and allocate them to allowable compartments.
# This is normal in fuel delivery systems where you have diesel/petrol constraints.
# We're just going to decide on which jobs may go in which compartments based on the
# index, and let's see if that's feasible. Obviously, you'll create it using proper logic
# based on the business rules.

for(i in 1:length(sr$model$jobs)){
  relations <- new (IVR8.Job.CompartmentRelation)
  relations$type <- 0  # 0 for inclusions, 1 for exclusions
  if(i %% 2 == 0){ # just an alternating pattern
    relations$compartmentIds <- paste0("c", c(1,3))
  }else{
    relations$compartmentIds <- paste0("c", c(2,4))
  }
  sr$model$jobs[[i]]$compartmentRelations <- relations # Set the compartment relation on the job
}

sr$model$jobs[[1]]$toString() %>% cat # Here you can see we have c2 and c4 as allowable compartments

# Now we can define a compartment set (a container for the individual compartments)
# which is attached to a vehicle.
cset <- new (IVR8.CompartmentSet)
cset$id <- 'tanker'
cset$compartmentIds <- paste0('c', 1:4) # Indicates that this compartment set has c1:c4 available
sr$model$compartmentSets <- cset # add it to the model

# Then we assign the "tanker" compartment set to the vehicle class.
# NOTE: We could have added it to each vehicle but this is easier.
sr$model$vehicleClasses[[1]]$compartmentSetId <- 'tanker'

# Set the other relevant information
sr$solveType <- 0 # 0 for optimise, 1 for evaluate, 2 for reoptimise

# View the model in plain-text format (string or JSON)
sr$model$toString() %>% cat
sr$model$toJSON() %>% cat

```

3. **Submit the model to the API**

```{r}
#| echo: true
#| output: false
requestID <- api %>% postSolveRequest(sr)  
```


4. **Retrieve the model response**

```{r}
#| echo: true
#| output: false
resp <- api %>% getResponse(requestID)
```

5. **Look at the result**

```{r}
#| echo: true
#| output: false

# Get the solve time
solveTime <- api %>% getSolveTime(requestID)
```

Solve time: `r solveTime`

```{r}
#| echo: true
#| output: true

resp$objective

# Tabulate the data in native-R format
tab <- resp %>% tabulate(sr)

# View the produced summary
tab$compartmentSummary

# The compartment summary is nice but it doesn't tell us whether we stuck to the constraints
# around the relations for each of the jobs.
# So let's build a dataframe of allowable compartments per job and join it to the normal response.
jdata<- do.call(rbind, lapply(sr$model$jobs,
              function(i){data.frame(id = i$id,
                          allowableCompartments =
                            paste0(i$compartmentRelations$compartmentIds, collapse = ','),
                          stringsAsFactors = F)}))

tab$nodes %>% select(taskId, compartmentId, jobId) %>% left_join(jdata, by = c('jobId' = 'id'))
# We can see that at each task assignment we only used compartments
# which were in the allowable set we provided to the API.
# It's probably worth noting that the default is all compartments in a compartment set are allowed
# so you can either specify an inclusive sub-set, or excluded sub-set.
# If all compartments are excluded then it will let you know that there's no feasible allocation.

# Plot the data (ggplot or leaflet)
resp %>% plotResponse(sr) # ggplot                       
resp %>% plotResponseLeaflet(sr) # leaflet (if it's mappable)
```
